source_refs.note: Exercise 3.4, Question 1: Exercise 3.4, book page 94: Q1-Q15 (integration by partial fractions); answers book pages 301-302

blocks.explanation:
A rational function whose denominator is already factorised into two different linear factors: Case-I.
The fraction is proper (degree 1 on top, degree 2 below), so no division is needed.
Plan: split into \(\frac{A}{x + 1} + \frac{B}{x + 2}\), find \(A\), \(B\) by putting the roots, then integrate each part to a logarithm.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{5x + 7}{(x + 1)(x + 2)}\,dx\).
To find: the integral.
Method: partial fractions, Case-I (non-repeated linear factors). Each factor \(x + a\) gets one fraction \(\frac{A}{x + a}\), and \(\int \frac{dx}{x + a} = \ln|x + a|\).

Write the partial fractions
\[\dfrac{5x + 7}{(x + 1)(x + 2)} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 2}\]
Why: The denominator has two different linear factors, so one constant over each factor.

Clear the fractions
\[5x + 7 = A(x + 2) + B(x + 1) \quad (1)\]
Why: Multiply both sides by \((x + 1)(x + 2)\). Equation (1) is true for every \(x\).

Integrate each fraction
\[\int \dfrac{5x + 7}{(x + 1)(x + 2)}\,dx\]
\[= 2\int \dfrac{dx}{x + 1} + 3\int \dfrac{dx}{x + 2}\]
\[= 2\ln|x + 1| + 3\ln|x + 2| + c\]
Why: \(\int \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx = \ln|f(x)|\); here \(f'(x) = 1\).

Check
\[\dfrac{2}{x + 1} + \dfrac{3}{x + 2} = \dfrac{2(x + 2) + 3(x + 1)}{(x + 1)(x + 2)}\]
\[= \dfrac{5x + 7}{(x + 1)(x + 2)} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Adding the partial fractions back gives the original integrand.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the answers at the end of the book (page 301), the answers of Exercise 3.4 are printed under the wrong heading "Exercise 3.6". The answer of this question is item (i) of that block: \(2\ln|x + 1| + 3\ln|x + 2| + c\). That answer is correct. The block headed "Exercise 3.4" (page 301) belongs to a different exercise.
